mohan: FYI intake for new model 'cerulean-9b' from third-party repo. They published weights + a short license PDF. Asking: can we host (hosted API + dedicated) and run int4 quantization experiments? Pinging legal + infra.

sophie: can you paste the license snippet? quick check before we run any benchmarks.

mohan: pasted excerpt from license:
```
Cerulean Model License v0.9
- Permitted: research use, internal evaluation
- Restricted: commercial hosting, redistribution without explicit commercial license
- Derivative works: allowed for non-commercial research only
```
Not super explicit about hosted endpoints. Link: https://example.org/cerulean/license

legal: quick take — this looks like a "non-commercial" restriction. That typically blocks public hosted API (paid or free with commercial terms). Dedicated/private (customer-managed infra) might be OK for internal/enterprise use but depends on whether customers' use counts as "commercial". Need to confirm two things:
1) does "commercial hosting" include SaaS where we charge customers for access? likely yes
2) derivative clause: if quantization modifies weights, that could be a derivative — license may forbid commercial derivative distribution.

alyssa: technical Q — quantizing will modify the matrix values. For int4/post-training quant we generally store transformed weights; depending on jurisdiction that may be derivative. For experiments we can run locally in our sandbox, but we should avoid shipping quantized weights or a quantized model binary until legal greenlight.

pat: infra notes: if legal says "no hosted", Dedicated + Private are possibilities but we need to ensure KMS + data isolation. ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-3241 for KMS checklist :lock:

sophie: from product perspective: if cerulean's license blocks hosted, we still want to know: (a) can we offer embeddings or generate outputs as a passthrough (i.e., we call their model hosted elsewhere) and (b) can we fine-tune on customer data? both matter for sales.

legal: actions I need from you to finalize:
- list of intended product surfaces (hosted API, embeddings, fine-tuning, reranking)
- whether we'll redistribute weights or only call model in-process
- whether customers will be charged for access (revenue)
- any model modifications (quant/tuning) and intended distribution
Once we have that I'll draft a short licensing memo and request a commercial license from the model authors if needed.

mohan: quick benchmark note from offline run (sandbox only): `cerulean-9b` PTQ int4 (GPTQ-like) vs fp16:
- SQuAD F1: fp16=88.3, int4=85.1 (drop ~3.2)
- Latency (p99 tokens): fp16=210ms, int4=130ms (~38% faster)
We saw increased hallucination on long-context summarization tests. Will add eval logs to the ticket.

alyssa: recommend gating policy:
- BLOCK hosted public API until commercial license clarifies hosting + derivative
- ALLOW internal evals and private/dedicated hosting if customers sign DPA and usage is enterprise-only (legal to confirm)
- NO redistribution of any modified weights until explicit permission

legal: agree. I'll open a request to the model maintainers asking for:
- commercial license for hosting
- clarification on derivative/quantization
- permission to redistribute quantized weights to paying customers (if they want on-prem bundles)

mohan: cool. I'll attach eval results, use-cases from product, and a short revenue/monetization note to INFRA-3241 and LEGAL-requests. Next update in this thread once we hear back. :pray:

ops-bot: ticket LEGAL-2027 created for license request to Cerulean authors
